processing: A green tea, fixed and then rolled into thin, straight needles and dried. Details vary by maker and little is recorded about the exact steps.
harvest_season: Spring only, usually a single picking in the year, taken early so that the shoots are small.
appearance_dry: Fine, small, straight strips that look like pine needles.
appearance_liquor: Bright and clear, typically a pale yellow-green.
appearance_wet: Small tender buds and leaves, as the early picking would suggest.
taste_profile: Clean, high aroma and a mellow, fresh cup with a green vegetable note.

brewing.notes: General advice for fine needle greens. These small shoots extract quickly, so start cooler and shorter than you would with a larger leaf.

vintage_note: Sold as the current year's spring harvest, since it is typically picked only once a year. Drink it within the year, as with other green teas.
description:
Anhua is known to most tea drinkers for dark tea, so a fine green tea from the same Hunan county comes as a surprise. Anhua Songzhen, pine needle tea, takes its name from its shape: small, thin, straight strips.

The size comes from early picking.

Expect a clean, high aroma and a mellow, fresh cup with a green vegetable edge. The fine shoots give up their flavour fast, so keep the water cool and the steeps moderate.

Do not confuse it with Anhua's dark teas, such as Qianliang and Fu brick, which are a different world altogether. Ask for this spring's harvest, because there is usually just the one each year.
history:
Anhua Songzhen is usually dated to 1959, when it was developed in the same period as Gaoqiao Yinfeng, reportedly as a gift for the tenth anniversary of the People's Republic. Claims for tea growing in Anhua go back much further, but they refer to the county in general and not to this tea.

It is sometimes grouped as one of China's three needle teas, with Nanjing Yuhua and Enshi Yulu.
